# defuss-search

> Hybrid search for JavaScript and TypeScript in the browser, Bun and Node.js. BM25 and vector retrieval run over the same documents and are fused into one ranking; a document whose symbol or ID equals the query ranks first, an optional ColBERT reranker refines the top 25, and every hit explains its rank. No search server; the root entry has no runtime dependencies. MIT license, version 0.5.0.

Use it when one search box must find exact strings (symbols, IDs, error codes, part numbers) and meaning (paraphrases, translations) in one ranked list, inside your app. It is not a hosted search service: it has no server, persistence, authentication or approximate nearest-neighbor index (see Limits).

## Measured

From this repository's benchmarks, version 0.5.0 (`make bench`, `bun run bench:strategies`, Bun 1.4.3, one thread). Recall@k (R@k) is the share of queries whose relevant document ranks in the top k.

- 92.5% R@1 and 97.3% R@5 for 1,000 questions in 20 languages over 2,000 passages (tiny-embedding-bench-v1, a Belebele subset), default fusion without a reranker. Bun, Node.js and Chromium return the same rank for every question.
- 98.0% R@1 for exact matches in 8,043 documentation sections (defuss-shadcn; each query uses a section's own words).
- 97.8% R@1 for notes searched in another language; BM25 alone reaches 22.0%.
- 93.6% R@1 on 500 held-out questions with the fusion settings tuned on 500 others; the gated reranker reaches the same R@1 (93.6%).
- Fusing and ranking 2,000 passages takes 0.8 ms per query once the query vector exists; model inference is extra.
- Model downloads: none for lexical-only search, 2.3 MB (Winzling-reranker) for the tiny factory, 28.8 MB (Winzling-embed) for the lexical-semantic factory, each as Brotli files decoded in the browser.

| Query set, R@1 / R@5 | Lexical-only | Tiny | Lexical-semantic |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Belebele, 1,000 questions, 20 languages | 90.3% / 97.3% | 90.6% / 96.7% | 92.5% / 97.3% |
| Notes found by their translations | 22.0% / 24.2% | 47.3% / 72.5% | 97.8% / 100.0% |
| Notes found by a paraphrase | 27.3% / 27.3% | 45.5% / 81.8% | 81.8% / 100.0% |
| API docs, exact matches | 98.0% / 98.0% | 98.0% / 98.0% | 98.0% / 98.0% |
| API docs, natural-language questions | 40.0% / 70.0% | 40.0% / 72.0% | 40.0% / 76.0% |

## Install

```sh
bun add defuss-search defuss-lexicalsearch defuss-vectorsearch
```

`pnpm add`, `npm install` and `yarn add` take the same packages. `defuss-lexicalsearch` and `defuss-vectorsearch` are optional peers: install the ones you use.

## Quick start

```js
import { apiSearchPreset } from 'defuss-lexicalsearch';
import { searchPreset } from 'defuss-search';
import { createHybridIndex } from 'defuss-search/indexing';

const search = createHybridIndex({
  documents: [
    { id: 'push', fields: { symbol: 'Array.prototype.push()', description: 'Add elements to the end of an array' } },
    { id: 'pop', fields: { symbol: 'Array.prototype.pop()', description: 'Remove the last element of an array' } },
  ],
  vectors: [[1, 0], [0, 1]],
  defaults: searchPreset('efficient'),
  lexical: apiSearchPreset,
  lexicalSearch: { exact: { fields: ['symbol'] } },
});
const hits = await search.search({ text: 'Array.prototype.push()', vector: [0, 1] }, {
  strategy: 'fusion', exact: 'promote',
});
console.log(hits[0].id); // "push": the exact match ranks first
```

## Choose

- Factories in `defuss-search/strategies`, each returning a `HybridSearch`: `createLexicalOnlySearch(index)` needs no model; `createLexicalSemanticTinySearch(index, { documents, colbert })` uses one 2.3 MB model; `createLexicalSemanticSearch(index, { documents, embedder, reranker })` uses Winzling-embed vectors and an optional ColBERT reranker. Start with lexical-only and add a model when translations or paraphrases matter.
- Presets: `searchPreset('efficient')` fuses without a reranker; pass it whenever no reranker is configured. `searchPreset('reranked')`, the default, needs a reranker; on the benchmark it matched efficient's R@1 (92.5%) and ran ColBERT for 893 of 1,000 questions.
- Retrieval: `strategy: 'fusion'` (default), `'vector-first'` or `'lexical-first'`. A cascade never adds candidates its first stage missed.
- Exact matches: `exact: 'promote'` with `lexicalSearch: { exact: { fields: [...] } }` ranks original-string matches first.
- Languages: one lexical analyzer per language field; pass the query's `language`, the package does not detect it.

## Entry points

| Entry | Exports |
| --- | --- |
| `defuss-search` | `HybridSearch`, `fuseRankings`, `searchPreset`, types |
| `defuss-search/indexing` | `createHybridIndex` |
| `defuss-search/strategies` | `createLexicalOnlySearch`, `createLexicalSemanticTinySearch`, `createLexicalSemanticSearch` |
| `defuss-search/lexical` | `createLexicalRetriever`, `withSurfaceFields`, `surfaceAnalyzer`, `surfaceField` |
| `defuss-search/vector` | `createVectorRetriever` |
| `defuss-search/colbert` | `createColbertAdapter`, `createColbertRetriever`, `buildColbertTokenIndex` |

ESM and CommonJS with TypeScript declarations. Importing the package downloads no model; the caller creates and disposes models.

## Results

- `rank` is the final order. Scores from different stages use different scales: never sort hits by score.
- Each hit carries its rank and raw score per source, the fusion contributions and the reasons for a promotion; `searchWithStats()` adds candidate counts, stage timings and the reranker decision.
- Shared `ids` eligibility restricts both sources before top-k.

## Limits

- No language detection, persistence, server, authentication, model download or embedding training.
- Vector search scores every eligible row (exact or TurboQuant codes); there is no approximate nearest-neighbor index, so query cost grows with the corpus.
- `createHybridIndex()` holds an immutable snapshot; rebuild it to update.
- Query and document vectors must come from the same model and preprocessing.
- An `AbortSignal` cannot interrupt a running ONNX call.
- The figures above hold for these fixtures. Model quality differs by language: the weakest of the 20, Hindi, reaches 70.0% R@1.
